Here is what I would tell them, in plain words:

Keep your papers in order all the time — license, registration, insurance where you can reach them without digging. That is not giving in. That is giving them nothing to use against you.

When it happens: both hands where they can see them from the first second. Say what you are going to do before you do it. 'My registration is in the glove box. Can I reach for it?' No move they did not expect.

Stay calm even when you are right and they are wrong. Your safety is worth more than winning the argument on the road. The conversation about what was fair can happen later, at home, with family.

Afterward: write it down while it is fresh — time, place, what was said, badge number if you can see it, who was nearby. Tell someone you trust right away. That record matters more than you think.

And tell them this is not new. Their grandfather knows that tight feeling. His father did too. What happened then and what they see now belong in the same conversation. Knowing the history does not make the stop easier, but it means they are not the first, and they are not carrying it alone.
